newsitem.title: USA: IMF outlines ways to help Albania, sets conditions.
newsitem.headline: IMF outlines ways to help Albania, sets conditions.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has outlined ways in which it might be able to help Albania recover from economic crisis, but laid down conditions which the government in Tirana would first have to meet.

A statement distributed at a donors' conference late last month and obtained in Washington on Wednesday said IMF help would start with "post-conflict emergency assistance," but a longer-term loan could be negotiated once conditions were in place.

This would include improving security in Albania, ensuring the government controlled the whole country, building up a satisfactory record of tax collection, winding up pyramid schemes and cutting the budget deficit.
The collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes earlier this year plunged Albania into months of violent unrest during which more than 1,500 people were killed.

"The IMF remains fully prepared to help Albania and looks forward to starting negotiations on financial assistance in support of a strong economic programme as soon as possible," the statement said, noting that IMF experts had already held extensive talks with the government in Tirana .

"We plan to send a full mission to Tirana in the next couple of weeks," the statement said. "This mission will be immediately followed by technical assistance missions in the areas of taxation and entral banking."
The IMF statement said an initial programme would aim to stabilise the Albanian economy and rebuild the institutions needed for a longer-term loan to go ahead.
"Some improvement in law and order and progress in dealing with the pyramid schemes will be needed for IMF support under emergency assistance to go ahead," it said.

"If all goes well -- and this requires decisive action by the Albanian authorities and strong cooperation by the donor community -- a programme supported by emergency assistance could be in place as early as October," it said.

Albanian Finance Minister Arben Malaj said on Tuesday that Tirana was determined to meet IMF demands to restore order, strengthen the financial system and imporve transparency on the pyramid investment schemes.
"After Bosnia and Georgia, we are the third country in the IMF history to benefit from such a programme and it is vital to convince foreign investors to invest in Albania," he said.
